record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: Let Q be the vertices of a regular three-dimensional n-gon in the plane x=1 centered at (1,0,0). For the union of all f^k(Q), k∈N, where f is a homothety centered at the origin with small scale factor λ, what is the corresponding Steiner-tree structure?

evidence.quote: Question 2.13. For a regular 3-dimensional n-gon in the plane x=1 centered at (1,0,0); let Q be the set of its vertices and consider the union of all f^k(Q), k∈N, where f is a homothety with the center in the origin and a small enough scale factor λ. What is the structure of the corresponding Steiner tree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 3 and a real number λ ∈ (0,1) (taken sufficiently small). In ℝ³, let Q ⊂ {x = 1} be the set of vertices of a regular planar n-gon lying in the plane x = 1, centered at the point (1, 0, 0). Let f : ℝ³ → ℝ³ be the homothety centered at the origin with ratio λ, i.e. f(p) = λ p, and define the (countably infinite) terminal set

  T = ⋃_{k=0}^{∞} f^k(Q) = { λ^k q : k ∈ ℕ, q ∈ Q } ⊂ ℝ³.

A Steiner tree for T is a connected set S ⊂ ℝ³ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff length containing T (allowing additional "Steiner" branching points). Describe, for sufficiently small λ, the combinatorial and geometric structure of a Steiner tree for T: specify the locations and degrees of the Steiner points, the topology of the tree, and how the structure depends on n (and possibly on λ).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent (2025) compilation of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers. No published resolution was found; related work treats Steiner trees on vertices of a single regular polygon and on infinite terminal sets on polygon sides, but the specific nonplanar self-similar configuration generated by iterated homothety of a regular 3-dimensional n-gon's vertices does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Question 2.13 asks for the structure of the Steiner tree for the union of iterated homotheties of the vertices of a regular n-gon.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open question in a 2025 problem list.

status_evidence.title: Steiner minimal trees for regular polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Steiner minimal trees for vertices of a single regular n-gon.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses only the single-polygon case, not the iterated-homothety nonplanar variant.

status_evidence.title: Steiner trees with infinitely many terminals on the sides of regular polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Considers Steiner trees with infinite terminal sets associated with regular polygons.
status_evidence.claim: The infinite-terminal regime is studied in different settings, but does not resolve the iterated 3D homothety case.
